key_insight: Biot–Savart-inspired activation functions improve incompressible-flow PINN accuracy without changing the conventional velocity–pressure formulation.
engineering_relevance: Flow-informed neural representations could improve simulations of wakes, vortices, and localized shear structures.
method: Extract a smooth rational activation profile from a regularized Biot–Savart kernel.
Test fixed-scale and learnable-scale activation variants.
Retain standard physics-informed training to isolate the activation’s influence.
evidence_signal: Across five flow benchmarks and 21 benchmark–architecture comparisons, fixed- and learnable-scale variants reduced combined velocity error versus tanh PINNs by averages of 31.7% and 33.2%, respectively.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish computational cost or generalization to high-Reynolds-number turbulent flows.
paper_title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
